Referred Sections: Discogenic Lower Back Pain/Degenerative Disc Disease (TOC: S8.1.3)

Medical necessity indications.Guideline Category: Discogenic Lower Back Pain/Degenerative Disc Disease
Required findings: Imaging findings: Plain x-rays and advanced imaging (CT or MRI) must demonstrate moderate to severe single-level disc degeneration at the requested surgical level(s).

Symptom duration and nature: Presence of chronic, unremitting, discogenic axial lower back pain and associated disability secondary to single-level degenerative lumbar disc disease for at least one year.
Functional impairment: Significant daily pain resulting in clinically significant functional impairment (e.g., inability to perform household chores, prolonged standing, etc.).

Conservative management: Structured, physician-supervised, multi-modal nonoperative management with licensed healthcare professionals including regularly scheduled appointments and follow-up evaluations, with less than clinically meaningful improvement after at least 12 consecutive months of at least TWO of the following (unless contraindicated): prescription strength analgesics/steroids/gabapentinoids/NSAIDs, provider-directed exercise program, epidural steroid injections/selective nerve root blocks at the same level(s), or facet joint injections/medial branch blocks/radiofrequency ablations.

Behavioral/mental health: Absence of unmanaged significant mental and/or behavioral health disorders (e.g., major depressive disorder, chronic pain syndrome, secondary gain, opioid and alcohol use disorders).

Nicotine status: Documentation of nicotine-free status as either a never-smoker, or refraining from smoking/smokeless tobacco/nicotine replacement therapy for at least six (6) weeks prior to surgery, validated by objective cotinine testing (serum, urinary, or saliva) within normal range.
